findings.obligation: Add no field that no accepted outcome reads, and give each fact one owner (nw-code-design-oo rule 7; nw-code-craftsmanship rule 2). The design's Decision for P3 prescribed the field: 'views::IssuePage gains title, description, status_slug and status_chip'.
findings.observation: IssuePage.status_slug is filled at comments.rs:758 from detail.state and never read: grep status_slug over crates/ returns only those two write sites; issue.html renders status_chip|safe and no slug, and the oracle reads the chip markup (span.state[data-state]) only. The same stored fact already has an owner on the page - the chip string whose data-state AND text are the slug - so the page carries one fact twice, and the field's own doc comment claims a reader ('so the page can be read for the stored value and not only for rendered markup') that does not exist. Dimension 1 over-engineering, severity Medium; no behaviour is wrong and no check fails.
findings.remediation: Amend the P3 decision to three fields (title, description, status_chip) and have the crafter delete status_slug from views.rs:1117 and comments.rs:758 with its doc comment, or name the reader that needs the bare slug and give it an observation in the oracle.

findings.obligation: The design names every shipped promise the Request must not break, so the crafter needs no discovery of its own (architecture.md's own constraint: 'Shipped promises this Request must not break').
findings.observation: The list names the no-html-wrapper body, the overlay dialog container, the rail-and-theme-control absence, the full-document sign-in and forgot pages, the issue heading, the chip data-state, the colour-token regions, the asset hashes, the user-menu link and the head-script attributes - and omits NFR-4 / ODD-8: crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/keyboard-shortcut-bindings.feature:115 'With scripting disabled the full-page keyboard help still works' locates the list by CSS class .keyboard-help (keyboard_shortcut_bindings.rs:2460, :2498, :2519, :4291). Nothing in the design told the new page arm to keep that class. The crafter found it independently and kept class=keyboard-help on keyboard_help_page.html, so the promise holds and that scenario is green in the reused CI run; the gap is in the authority, not in the behaviour. Severity Medium: a later page arm built from this design alone would drop the class.
findings.remediation: Add the no-JS full-page help promise (NFR-4 / ODD-8, found by .keyboard-help) to the shipped-promises constraint, and state there that the page arm keeps the class and deliberately omits role and aria-label.

findings.obligation: One word names one concept across code, tests and docs; a changed document agrees with the code and is unambiguous to its reader (nw-code-design-oo section 3; nw-code-craftsmanship rules 38-39).
findings.observation: This feature published three ADRs into the shared product ADR directory under two naming schemes: ADR-BARE-PAGES-001.md (feature-prefixed, as ADR-NAV-POLISH-003.md, ADR-IIS-SKR-002.md and the rest of that directory are) and the unqualified ADR-002.md and ADR-003.md. Unqualified 'ADR-002' and 'ADR-003' already denote OTHER features' local ADRs throughout the repository, including on the very route this Request changes: keyboard_shortcut_bindings.rs:85-87 cites 'ADR-003' for the overlay host, feature_pwa_mobile.rs:10 and :654 cite 'ADR-003' and 'ADR-002' for mobile emulation and the PWA manifest, base.html cites 'pwa-mobile-rendering slice 03 (ADR-002)'. The new code comments disambiguate by writing 'ui-bare-pages ADR-002', but the file names do not, and ADR-002.md carries 'Status: Superseded by BARE-PAGES-001' while BARE-PAGES-001 states 'Everything ADR-002 decided stands' and the production code cites ADR-002 as live authority - so a reader of the file alone reads a current decision as withdrawn. Severity Low; no behaviour is affected.
findings.remediation: Rename the two ADRs to the directory's feature-prefixed scheme (ADR-BARE-PAGES-002/003 or equivalent), update the citing comments in keyboard.rs, views.rs, card_page.html and keyboard_help_page.html in the same change, and record ADR-002's status as amended-by rather than superseded-by while its decision still stands.

findings.obligation: Every declared behaviour of a law has an executable stimulus and assertion. L4 declares two clauses: the eight named inputs carry exactly their token, AND 'no other input in the repository carries a token this Request added'.
findings.observation: The scenario reads the eight named inputs plus one negative row (the forgotten-password email). Nothing in the oracle observes the second clause: no step enumerates the repository's other inputs, so a token added to a ninth input would leave this lane green. I verified the clause myself by reading the diff and grepping crates/foundry-app/templates (only the eight gained a token; the autocomplete=off inputs in integrations/ and the lane modals are pre-existing and untouched), so there is no defect in the candidate - the gap is in the evidence, and it is latent for the next change. Severity Low, non-blocking.
findings.remediation: Either narrow L4 in the design to the eight named inputs and keep the negative row as the only exclusion read, or add one read over the served markup of the pages this Request touches that asserts no input outside the eight declares a token.

No test path beyond the recorded oracle was added or changed: the candidate's only test-side files are the designer's own feature file, its step module and the two one-line registrations, and no shipped scenario was weakened, narrowed or skipped. Oracle quality: no testing theater found - every step guards its population before asserting (assert_answered_something, row counts, field counts, non-empty page type), expected values are written in the feature file rather than read back off the render, the escaping reference is computed in the test, the card is read from what the browser paints rather than from a class name, and both browser waits are bounded.
